correctness.rationale: For any unselected edge and any selected edge the distance is exactly a two-valued function of root-edge intersection, so failure of equidistance is exactly the occurrence of complementary incidence signatures. Every simple three-edge root graph belongs to one of five listed types. Two are proven positive only at explicit small orders and each negative type has explicit complement-witness pairs over its remaining range. The no-two-landmark argument and exact labeled triangle, path-plus-edge and matching counts finish the proof. A separately coded BFS checker agrees on every two/three-set candidate over thirteen original graphs, not merely generated patterns.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The scalar result is strictly weaker: it says at least one minimum set exists and forbids smaller sets. It neither rules out other minimum 3-sets nor counts them. The old Johnson resolving-number result maximizes landmark sets failing to resolve, a different universal/separation quantifier; its known counts of equidistant vertices for fixed pairs do not classify three-landmark minimum equalizer families. The present case-by-case root-edge classification supplies the missing implication.

originality.rationale: Claim assessed is the full basis classification and labeled multiplicity, not the previously known equidistant dimension. The relevant 2024 primary full text gives scalar dimension three for Johnson and Kneser graphs and one triangle construction, but no exhaustively quantified minimizing-family theorem; case analysis here proves the additional 5/6 exceptional orbits and threshold 7. Equivalent graph names, duality, known tables, and stronger coverage were queried. Residual alternate-terminology priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The published 2024 theorem establishes exact minimum sizes but leaves the natural optimizer structure unenumerated. Here a full infinite-parameter optimizer classification proves eventual triangle rigidity at order seven and two qualitatively different small-order exceptional orbits, with exact labeled counts and a simultaneous Johnson/Kneser equality through complement-distance duality. This identifies all minimum anonymity-equidistance landmark placements and is a structurally motivated complete problem, not an arbitrary narrow numerical slice.
